text:
julia.s: quick q — we're onboarding a customer that wants AKV in a partner tenant. can an assigned user/mi from our tenant rewrap DEKs in their vault, or do we need cross-tenant service principal + admin consent?
sam.k: you can't use a user-assigned MI from our tenant to access a vault in another tenant. need either cross-tenant SP or a managed identity provisioned in their tenant.
mica: for clarity: two patterns — 1) federated identity (workload identity) + AKV RBAC in customer tenant, 2) customer creates an MI and grants it access. both require tenant-level cooperation.
oj: infra-bot: NOTE: "subscription/tenant boundary enforced by Azure; MSI tokens scoped to home tenant" :info: 
julia.s: ok — what's the minimum privilege for rotation jobs we run? we want least privilege for rewrap + list/get/decrypt for envelope keys.
sam.k: rotation job needs get and unwrapKey on the KEK, and wrapKey for re-encrypt back. for DEKs stored elsewhere you need encrypt/decrypt depending on flow. prefer RBAC Key permissions: UnwrapKey, WrapKey, Get.
mica: also need KeyVault Secrets Get if DEK is stored as a secret object, or Blob access if DEK in storage. check how the customer stores envelope keys.
omar: audit/logging question — how do we ensure rewraps are visible in their audit logs and forwarded to our SIEM? suggestions?
sam.k: enable Diagnostic Settings on the AKV resource -> send to Log Analytics / Event Hub. event hub -> our ingestion. make sure to include AuditEvent and KeyVaultAuditEvents.
mica: sample az cli snippet:
```
az monitor diagnostic-settings create \ 
  --resource-id /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault> \ 
  --name send-to-eh \ 
  --event-hub-name <eh-name> \ 
  --workspace <log-analytics-id> \ 
  --logs '[{"category":"AuditEvent","enabled":true}]'
```
sec-oncall: FYI re: incident play — if a KEK is suspected compromised, immediate steps: 1) rotate KEK in customer tenant, 2) mark previous KEK as disabled, 3) run rewrap for active DEKs, 4) update key IDs in metadata and rotate consumer tokens. doc: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/akv-key-compromise 
julia.s: do we have a dry-run mode for rewraps? want to validate we can re-encrypt without impacting old tokens and with minimal downtime.
omar: yes — we do a non-destructive rewrap: create new key version, rewrap DEK copies to new KEK, keep old key enabled until all consumers switched. we run on canary DEKs first.
sam.k: edge-case: cross-tenant key import — if customer imported a key (HSM-protected) with export disabled, rewrap still works server-side but key material can't leave vault. confirm their keys are not non-exportable if they planned out-of-vault ops.
mica: logging trap: Event categories sometimes show 'KeyOperation' vs 'SecretOperation' depending on how DEK stored. make sure DiagnosticSettings includes both. Also check resource provider errors — 403 vs 401 differ.
deploy-bot: deploy status: rotation-runner v2.3 queued for canary at 2024-09-15T21:12:00Z.
julia.s: one more — RBAC vs access policies for partner tenants: which should we ask customers to use?
sam.k: prefer RBAC (Azure RBAC) for new vaults — it's centralized and friendlier for federated identities. Access policies are legacy and can conflict with RBAC if not migrated. If their tenant is older, they might still be on access policies.
omar: migration note: switching from access policies to RBAC can be disruptive unless you run a migration plan: map policies -> role assignments, test, then disable policies. mention this in onboarding checklist.
mica: action items: @julia.s create onboarding checklist item: "Confirm AKV auth pattern (RBAC vs AccessPolicy), DiagnosticSettings target, who owns EH/LA, key exportability, canary DEKs".
julia.s: thanks — I'll ping customer and get answers. tagging @sec-oncall for runbook review after I have customer answers. :thumbsup:
sec-oncall: ack — I'll review the runbook and add emergency rollback steps for cross-tenant TF failures.
